title: Upstream bug: bd export includes wisps in JSONL by default
description: Security review (P0.2) verified that bd export does NOT exclude wisps by default. 'wisp' is not in DefaultInfraTypes() at export_auto.go:163. The pre-commit hook passes no --exclude-type flag. Wisps (including error and escalation subtypes with stack traces) go into JSONL, into git, and potentially into Linear. This contradicts PLAN.md's privacy claim and the intended privacy boundary. File upstream at gastownhall/beads.

title: Implement external_ref storage separation (.beads/external_refs.json)
description: Implement the two-file separation design from PLAN.md §5 (post-adversarial-review). CI worker writes external_refs.json (bead_id → linear_id/url mapping); devs never touch it. CI workflow triggers only on issues.jsonl changes. Resolves: (1) external_ref write-back cycle (Arch C1), (2) CI self-triggering loop (Arch C2), (3) daily JSONL merge conflicts (Perf W1). See PLAN.md §5 'External_ref storage separation' for the full design.

title: Upstream bug: bd export includes memories in JSONL
description: Security review (P0.3/F-04) found that bd remember memories leak through the export pipeline. Memories contain potentially sensitive agent context, debugging notes, and personal observations that should not reach git or Linear. Same root cause as the wisp leak — DefaultInfraTypes() doesn't include 'memory'. File upstream at gastownhall/beads.

title: Open PR-4: issueBatchCreate and issueBatchUpdate adoption
description:
Implement tracker.BatchPushTracker interface (already defined at internal/tracker/types.go:62-65) on linear.Tracker. Add BatchCreate and BatchUpdate on linear.Client emitting issueBatchCreate (50/call) and issueBatchUpdate. Engine routes through BatchPush() when implemented. Graceful degradation: if a batch call fails, fall back to per-issue mutations for that batch.

**ARCHITECTURE BLOCKER** — required for efficient centralized writer. See PLAN.md §6 PR-4 for full scope.

## Acceptance criteria

- 50 issues push as 1 mutation, not 50
- Partial-failure batch (5 errors out of 50) falls back to single mutations for the 5 failures
- Smaller pushes (<50 issues) work via existing path
- Mock GraphQL test with batch response
- Charter-compliance noted (efficiency improvement of existing surface)

## Non-goals

- Not adding batch comments (Linear doesn't support)
- Not parallelizing multiple batches (sequential is fine for now)

title: Adopt centralized Linear sync architecture (Option 7)
description:
Implement the per-laptop reads + central CI writer architecture documented in PLAN.md §5. Replaces the current per-laptop bidirectional sync model with one CI-mediated single writer to Linear and per-laptop read-only pulls. Eliminates conflict thrash, duplicate creation, and rate-limit storms on the write path.

Key design decisions resolved:
- External_ref storage separation: CI writes .beads/external_refs.json, devs write .beads/issues.jsonl (PLAN.md §5)
- Bidirectional pull: PM-created Linear issues appear in devs' beads (decision d11)
- Disappearance policy: archive Linear issue when bead leaves JSONL (decision d12)
- Conflict policy: --prefer-linear on pulls (decision d5)
- Pull cadence: 15-min jittered cron (decision d8)

Depends on four architecture-blocker upstream PRs (PR-1, PR-3, PR-4, PR-5) under epic-upstream, plus the P0 security fix (PR-1) and privacy fix (wisp/memory leak bugs).

## Success criteria

- All 50 devs run bd linear sync --pull only locally (never push)
- One CI workflow is the sole bd linear sync --push invoker
- One OAuth client credential held in CI secrets, no personal API keys in any git-tracked file
- Every push to Linear is logged with bead_id, linear_id, outcome
- Sync success rate >= 99.5% over 50 consecutive runs in pilot
- Bead disappearance triggers Linear issue archival
- PM-created Linear issues flow to dev laptops on pull

title: Open PR-3: OAuth client-credentials support for linear.Client
description:
New file internal/linear/oauth.go implementing OAuth client-credentials grant against Linear's token endpoint. New config keys linear.oauth_client_id, linear.oauth_client_secret (yaml-only). Modify internal/linear/client.go to send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` when OAuth is configured, fall back to personal-key behavior otherwise. Token caching with 30-day TTL and auto-refresh on 401.

**ARCHITECTURE BLOCKER** — required for the centralized CI writer to run as actor=app. See PLAN.md §6 PR-3 for full scope.

## Acceptance criteria

- OAuth-configured client sends Bearer token on requests
- 401 triggers token refresh
- Personal API key path unchanged when OAuth not configured
- Mock OAuth token endpoint in internal/linear/oauth_test.go
- Roundtrip test with OAuth-configured client
- Cross-version migration test passes

## Non-goals

- Not implementing OAuth authorization-code flow (only client-credentials)
- Not implementing per-scope token requests

title: Upstream PRs to gastownhall/beads to unblock org architecture
description:
Coordinate the nine PRs documented in PLAN.md §6 plus two upstream bug reports. Each PR is independently valuable to the upstream project but several are blockers for the org's centralized architecture (epic-arch). Sequenced to land canary first (build reviewer trust) before architecture-critical PRs.

Critical path PRs (blocking pilot):
- PR-1 (refuse git-tracked secrets) — P0 security, unblocks safe per-laptop credentials
- PR-3 (OAuth client-credentials) — unblocks centralized writer credential
- PR-4 (batch mutations) — unblocks efficient writer (now parallel with PR-3)
- PR-5 (idempotency) — unblocks reliable writer

Independent PRs (land in any order):
- PR-0 (type mapping canary) — builds reviewer trust
- PR-2 (federation privacy) — fixes wisp leak in federation
- PR-6 (Retry-After) — rate-limit safety
- PR-7 (concurrency lock) — sync serialization
- PR-8 (audit log) — sync forensics

Upstream bugs:
- Wisp leakage in bd export (btl-16t)
- Memory leakage in bd export (btl-wqv)

## Success criteria

- PR-0 merged (reviewer trust established)
- PR-1 merged (P0 security closed)
- PR-3 merged (architecture unblocked)
- PR-4 merged (efficiency unblocked)
- PR-5 merged (reliability unblocked)
- PR-6 merged (rate-limit safety)
- Upstream bugs filed and acknowledged

title: Open PR-5: idempotency markers on Linear issue creation
description:
Generate a deterministic content hash per bead at creation time using only immutable fields: sha256(beads_id + creator_email + creation_timestamp_ns)[:12]. (Do NOT include title — title is mutable and would break idempotency on rename.) Embed in Linear description as <!-- bd-idempotency: <hash> -->.

Pre-create dedup query: use issues(filter: {description: {contains: "<marker>"}}) against the target team (validated 2026-05-02 in sandbox — see PLAN.md §9 d13). If found, link existing as external_ref instead of creating duplicate.

ARCHITECTURE BLOCKER — solves duplicate creation under sync interruption. See PLAN.md §6 PR-5 for full scope.

## Acceptance criteria

- Hash formula uses only immutable fields (beads_id + creator_email + creation_ts_ns) — NOT title
- Dedup query uses issues(filter: {description: {contains: "<marker>"}}) — NOT searchIssues (exact match, no indexing delay)
- Sync interrupted between create and external_ref update; re-run sync detects existing Linear issue via marker, links it, no duplicate created
- Two devs creating beads with the same content: second push finds and links the first
- Roundtrip test with mock GraphQL
- Backward-compatible: existing Linear issues without markers still match via existing logic

## Non-goals

- Not changing the marker format (HTML comment is the interoperable choice)
- Not exposing the marker as a beads field

title: Open PR-1: refuse to write linear.api_key to git-tracked config.yaml
description:
Detect git tracking of .beads/config.yaml in SetYamlConfig before writing yaml-only secret keys. Refuse with actionable error pointing to env var or out-of-tree secrets file. Update cmd/bd/init_templates.go:79-82 (stale documentation). Update examples/linear-workflow/README.md and docs/CONFIG.md to lead with env var. Add bd doctor check for git-tracked secret keys.

P0 SECURITY — addresses the verified credential-leak-on-default-path. See PLAN.md §6 PR-1 for full scope.

## Acceptance criteria

- bd config set linear.api_key foo in a git repo fails with helpful error
- bd doctor flags any git-tracked secret keys present in config.yaml
- bd doctor content scanning: scan tracked config files for patterns matching API keys (lin_api_*, Bearer *, etc.) — surface as P0 finding
- Template documentation updated to remove the false 'stored in the database' claim
- README and CONFIG.md lead with LINEAR_API_KEY env var
- Test coverage for tracked vs untracked config files
- Charter-compliance noted in PR description (security hygiene of existing flow)
- --force-git-tracked escape hatch for tests

## Non-goals

- Not changing where untracked config.yaml stores keys
- Not implementing the secrets.yaml file (separate concern)

title: CI monitoring/alerting dashboard for sync worker
description: Build monitoring dashboard tracking: sync success rate, push/pull counts, conflict frequency, API quota utilization, drift count (beads in JSONL vs Linear issues), latency per sync run. Wire alerting for: sync failure, rate limit breach, drift exceeding threshold.

title: JSONL merge strategy and .gitattributes config
description: Three reviewers (Arch H1, Flows E1, Perf W1) independently flagged JSONL text merge as the daily friction point. Git's default line-based merge works at the JSONL line level (one issue per line) but can produce invalid merges when two devs modify the same issue. Define the merge strategy: (a) union merge driver (both lines kept, CI worker dedup), (b) custom bead-aware merge driver, or (c) accept and document the manual resolution workflow. Configure .gitattributes accordingly.
close_reason: Shipped: .gitattributes with union merge + docs/merge-strategy.md committed to main

title: Spike: verify OAuth token acquisition race under concurrent CI
description: Security review (F-06) flagged that concurrent CI runs could invalidate each other's OAuth tokens. Linear's OAuth client-credentials grant issues one active token per app — fetching a new token might invalidate the previous one. If two CI runs both detect an expired token simultaneously, they could race on token refresh. Validate this behavior before building PR-3 (OAuth support). Test in the sandbox workspace.

title: Phase 1 pilot validation plan (50-bead burn-in, exit criteria tracking)
description: Define the structured validation plan for Phase 1 pilot per PLAN.md §8. Track exit criteria: 50+ beads pushed, zero unresolved errors over 20 consecutive runs, 2+ conflicts encountered and resolved, pilot devs report no disruption. Create the tracking artifacts and daily check scripts.

title: Decide: per-laptop pull credential strategy
description:
See PLAN.md §9 Open Decision #3.

**Resolved (2026-05-01)**: option (a) — personal Linear API key per developer, exported as LINEAR_API_KEY env var only. Migrate to OAuth client-credentials (option c) once PR-3 ships and Linear's OAuth scope model supports per-process scoping cleanly.

Reasoning: (a) is the minimum viable today and matches the auth method developers are already familiar with from Linear's UI. (b) creates a shared-secret rotation problem. (c) is the long-term clean answer.

## Acceptance criteria

- Decision documented in this bead (above)
- Communicated to all pilot devs (becomes part of task-runbook content)
- Pre-commit hook updated by PR-1 to enforce the chosen mechanism (block if linear.api_key in config.yaml)
close_reason: Resolved: option (a) — personal Linear API key per developer in LINEAR_API_KEY env var. Migrate to OAuth client-credentials once PR-3 ships. See bead description and PLAN.md §9 #3.

title: Open PR-2: federation respects ephemeral / wisp filters
description:
Add federation.exclude_types config key (default ['wisp']). In internal/storage/dolt/federation.go, filter the issue stream before federation push using the same predicate as engine.go:1295-1325. Multi-peer integration test.

**P1 PRIVACY** — closes the verified gap that wisps excluded from Linear push leak to federation peers. See PLAN.md §6 PR-2 for full scope.

## Acceptance criteria

- Wisp created on peer A does not appear on peer B after `bd federation sync`
- federation.exclude_types config key documented and defaulted to ['wisp']
- CHANGELOG.md entry calls out the behavior change
- Opt-out via federation.exclude_types = [] works
- Cross-version migration test passes

## Non-goals

- Not changing federation conflict resolution
- Not adding label-based federation filtering (separate scope)

title: Open PR-6: Retry-After header parsing and adaptive backoff
description:
In internal/linear/client.go:163-197, parse X-RateLimit-* headers and Retry-After. Prefer server-hint delay over computed exponential backoff when present. Circuit breaker: pause sync when remaining quota drops below linear.rate_limit_floor (default 100). Address the thundering-herd retry amplification pattern from GH#3623.

See PLAN.md §6 PR-6 for full scope.

## Acceptance criteria

- Mock 429 response with Retry-After: 30 → next request waits 30s, not computed backoff
- Circuit breaker pauses sync when remaining quota <100
- Behavior unchanged when headers absent
- SyncStats surfaces circuit-breaker activation as a warning

## Non-goals

- Not implementing per-endpoint rate limit tracking (Linear doesn't expose enough headers)
- Not implementing token bucket on the client side (server enforces)

title: Decide: per-laptop pull conflict resolution policy
description:
See PLAN.md §9 Open Decision #5.

**Resolved (2026-05-01)**: option (a) — `--prefer-linear`.

Reasoning: the CI worker's writes are authoritative; per-laptop pulls accept Linear's version on conflict. Any other choice creates the silent-overwrite failure mode the architecture exists to prevent. Devs who need to override Linear can do so by editing locally and pushing through git, which the CI worker will then push to Linear in the normal way.

## Acceptance criteria

- Policy documented (above)
- task-pull-cron's install-pull-cron.sh and CI worker invocations both pass `--prefer-linear`
close_reason: Resolved: option (a) — --prefer-linear. See bead description and PLAN.md §9 #5.

title: Spike: provision Linear OAuth app and validate actor=app behavior
description:
Workspace admin action: create OAuth app at Linear's developer portal in the sandbox workspace (https://linear.app/kevglynn), enable client_credentials grant. Test fetching a token, making an actor=app mutation, observing the resulting issue history attribution. Validate that dynamic rate limits scale per Cluster B's documentation.

Validates the assumption underlying PR-3 (OAuth client-credentials) before that PR is opened.

## Acceptance criteria

- OAuth app exists in sandbox, client_credentials grant enabled
- Successfully fetch access token via curl
- Create test issue with actor=app, verify creator displays as the app, not a user
- Document the workspace's actual rate limit ceiling from response headers
- Findings noted in this bead's resolution and in PLAN.md appendix

## Non-goals

- Not productionizing the credential (that's task-ci-worker)
- Not implementing token refresh in code (that's task-pr3)

title: Open PR-0 to gastownhall/beads: type mapping completion (canary)
description:
Add label-to-type mappings for decision, spike, story, milestone in internal/linear/mapping.go. Update linear.label_type_map.* defaults. Roundtrip tests for each new type. Closes upstream GH#3604. See PLAN.md §6 PR-0 for full scope.

## Acceptance criteria

PR opened against gastownhall/beads main, references GH#3604, includes unit tests in internal/linear/mapping_test.go, includes roundtrip test extension in cmd/bd/linear_roundtrip_test.go, passes `go test -race`, passes `golangci-lint`, charter-compliance noted in PR description.

## Non-goals

- Not changing default mappings for existing types
- Not introducing config surface beyond linear.label_type_map.*

title: Build CI worker for centralized Linear push (org-internal)
description:
Create .github/workflows/linear-sync.yml (or org's equivalent). Triggers on push events to main that touch .beads/issues.jsonl (NOT .beads/external_refs.json — see PLAN.md §5 external_ref storage separation). Steps: bd import from JSONL → bd linear sync --push --json → write .beads/external_refs.json → commit external_refs.json back to main → archive sync_history JSON. OAuth client-credentials in CI secrets. Lives in beads-to-linear repo (org-internal, not upstream).

## Acceptance criteria

- Workflow triggers only on .beads/issues.jsonl changes (not external_refs.json)
- Concurrency group serializes runs: `concurrency: { group: linear-sync-${{ github.repository }}, cancel-in-progress: false }`
- No self-triggering loop: CI commits to external_refs.json which does NOT trigger the workflow
- Workflow runs end-to-end on a no-op push event
- Push event with new bead creates issue in Linear
- Push event with bead update updates Linear
- External_refs written to .beads/external_refs.json (format per PLAN.md §5)
- sync_history JSON archived as CI artifact
- Failed runs surface via existing CI alerting
- Push-volume sanity check: refuse to push if delta exceeds configurable threshold (default 100 issues) — prevents accidental floods
- Bead disappearance handling: when a bead is in external_refs.json but absent from issues.jsonl, archive the corresponding Linear issue (decision d12)
- README documents trigger behavior, CI secrets required, and concurrency behavior

## Non-goals

- Not implementing webhook-style triggers (charter forbids upstream; org choice for org-internal)
- Not implementing parallel workers (sequential is fine until throughput is a problem)
- Not modifying bd export or issues.jsonl format

title: Handle Linear issue hard-deletion (404 on update) in sync
description: When a Linear issue is permanently deleted (not just archived), the next CI push attempt for that bead gets a 404. Current behavior is undefined — likely an unhandled error that halts the sync run. Define the behavior: (a) clear external_ref and re-create, (b) log warning and skip, (c) surface error for human review.

title: Branch protection rules for repos using beads-to-Linear sync
description: Configure branch protection on main to: require PR reviews, prevent force-push (protects JSONL and external_refs.json history), allow the CI bot to push external_refs.json commits. Document required GitHub settings.

title: Offboarding procedures for departed devs
description: When a dev leaves the org: revoke their LINEAR_API_KEY, remove their pull cron, reassign their in-progress beads, verify no orphaned Linear issues attributed to their account. Document in runbook.

title: Decide: multi-repo CI worker topology
description: When multiple repos use beads with Linear sync, does each repo run its own CI worker (simple, isolated, N workflows), or does a central worker aggregate across repos (complex, one workflow, cross-repo visibility)? This decision affects Phase 3+ expansion. Not blocking for pilot.

title: Config template for org Linear sync defaults
description: Create templates/.beads/config.yaml with org-specific defaults: linear.team_ids, linear.exclude_labels, linear.priority_map.*, linear.state_map.* defaults committed for consistency across devs. Include validation script to check dev configs against org template.

title: Dev onboarding guide for beads-to-Linear sync
description: Separate from the ops runbook (btl-pjn). Covers the dev perspective: how to set up LINEAR_API_KEY, install the pull cron, what to expect in bd list, how to handle merge conflicts on issues.jsonl, FAQ for common issues. Written for devs who are new to beads or new to the Linear integration.

title: Open PR-8: persistent sync audit log
description:
New Dolt table linear_sync_history. Persist SyncResult per run with per-issue outcome, errors, timing. Surface via bd linear history subcommand.

See PLAN.md §6 PR-8 for full scope.

## Required table fields

- sync_run_id (UUID)
- started_at, completed_at (timestamps)
- direction (push/pull/both)
- Per-issue rows: bead_id, linear_id, attempt_number, outcome (created/updated/skipped/failed/archived), status_code, duration_ms
- Before/after values for changed fields (enables rollback scripting)
- Error message (if failed)
- Total summary: issues_created, issues_updated, issues_failed, issues_archived

## Acceptance criteria

- bd linear sync writes a row per sync run to linear_sync_history with all required fields above
- Per-issue outcome rows include before/after values for changed fields
- bd linear history --since=2026-05-01 returns prior sync runs with summary
- bd linear history --detail <run-id> shows per-issue outcomes
- make test-upgrade passes (cross-version migration of new table)
- Rollback script can read history and generate compensating mutations

## Non-goals

- Not implementing log compaction (separate concern)
- Not exposing history via CLI filters beyond --since and --detail

title: Build per-laptop pull cron installer (org-internal)
description:
Create scripts/install-pull-cron.sh that installs a per-developer cron job for `bd linear sync --pull` with jitter. Validates LINEAR_API_KEY env var presence. Refuses to install if linear.api_key is set in .beads/config.yaml (defense-in-depth complement to PR-1).

## Acceptance criteria

- install-pull-cron.sh installs cron job
- Cron job runs `bd linear sync --pull --prefer-linear` with random sleep up to 180s for jitter (15-min cadence per decision-pull-cadence)
- Refuses install if linear.api_key in config.yaml
- uninstall command removes cron job
- Documented in docs/onboarding/

## Non-goals

- Not building a daemon (cron is sufficient)
- Not building a per-laptop UI for managing the cron

title: Open PR-7: per-workspace concurrency lock on bd linear sync
description:
Acquire .beads/.linear-sync.lock at start of `bd linear sync` to serialize concurrent invocations. SIGTERM releases cleanly. Document the lock contract.

See PLAN.md §6 PR-7 for full scope.

## Acceptance criteria

- Two concurrent `bd linear sync` invocations: one acquires lock, second waits or fails-fast (configurable)
- `go test -race ./internal/linear` passes
- Stale lock detection (lock holder died without releasing)

## Non-goals

- Not implementing distributed lock for multi-machine sync (single-workspace scope only)

title: Decide: per-laptop pull cadence
description:
See PLAN.md §9 Open Decision #8.

**Resolved (2026-05-01)**: option (a) — 15-min cron with jitter (random sleep up to 180s).

Reasoning: 15 minutes is well within agent-workflow tolerances; reduces aggregate pull traffic to comfortable levels. Charter forbids webhooks so sub-minute reads are not available; the trade-off is between read latency and aggregate pull traffic.

## Acceptance criteria

- Cadence decision documented (above)
- task-pull-cron's install-pull-cron.sh implements 15-min cadence with jitter
close_reason: Resolved: option (a) — 15-min cron with jitter (random sleep up to 180s). See bead description and PLAN.md §9 #8.

title: Write Linear sync operations runbook (org-internal)
description:
Create docs/runbooks/linear-sync.md covering: adding a new dev, offboarding a dev, rotating OAuth credentials, handling Linear API outage, debugging a sync conflict, adding a new Linear team, recovering from 'we synced 50,000 bad updates', reading the sync audit log.

## Acceptance criteria

- Each scenario in the description has a step-by-step section
- Each section references specific commands, file paths, and expected outputs
- New devs can complete onboarding from the runbook alone

## Non-goals

- Not duplicating bd's own documentation (link to it)
- Not writing per-team customizations (org runbook only)

title: Build Jira → Linear → beads backfill script (org-internal)
description:
Create scripts/jira-to-linear-backfill.sh orchestrating the 5-step sequence in PLAN.md §8: Linear's native Jira import, stabilize, beads create-only push, beads ↔ Linear external_ref reconciliation, switch to bidirectional. Includes dry-run mode.

Scope per decision-backfill-scope: all open Jira issues + last 12 months of closed; older closed stays in Jira archive.

## Acceptance criteria

- Dry-run mode previews each step's actions
- Live mode runs the full sequence with confirmation prompts between steps
- Idempotent (re-running picks up where it left off)
- Documented usage in docs/runbooks/

## Non-goals

- Not implementing reverse migration (Linear → Jira)
- Not handling per-team customizations of the import (manual step)
